analysis: Examined base_text for provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/ProviderLoop+InferenceHandler.swift (lines 1-1143). The PR changes only two lines. At line 135 (throwIfRefusingNewLocalWork) and line 513 (the authoritative pre-accept autopilot check in handleInferenceRequest), the call autopilotAllowsModel(modelId) is replaced by autopilotServesModel(modelId). The surrounding gates are unchanged: the autopilotCommand != nil check, autopilotManagesResidency with a missing modelSlots entry (503), the drain, shutdown and MTP checks, decrypt and sender-key validation, response encryption fail-closed (T-008, lines 797-842), and cache-scope plumbing from the coordinator-authenticated remoteCache.scope (T-041). Neither function's implementation is supplied, so I cannot verify whether autopilotServesModel is stricter or looser than autopilotAllowsModel. One possibility is that it also admits models that are not selected but are resident, such as models in a retirement or drop window. These gates are availability and placement policy for provider-owned autopilot residency. They are not authorization, attestation or encryption controls. App Attest serving authorization (TB-011/T-053) and coordinator routing remain authoritative, and network requests for non-resident models are still rejected when autopilot manages residency. Cancellation and reservation unwinding after these checks are unchanged. Plausible worst case: wrong admission produces a 503 capacity reroute, or work is admitted for a model that autopilot is retiring. This is availability only, with no identified confidentiality or billing impact. The integration pass should check the autopilotServesModel definition, likely in a ProviderLoop autopilot extension, for semantic equivalence. It should also confirm that no unload races with an admitted request; the requestToModel pin at line 528 mitigates eviction. No security regression was identified from the supplied evidence.
